messages:
Aisha (AE): ShadowBank confirmed POC start Wed. They do TLS inspection at the perimeter and need an allowlist + a short Q for their security packet: can we give static egress IPs and a minimal fw snippet? Also they asked whether PrivateLink will work with DPI. @Tom please advise.

Tom (Solutions): Short answer: yes, with caveats. PrivateLink (interface EPs) keeps traffic off the public internet from the customer side, but our backend still egresses from Redwood-managed IPs. If their DPI terminates TLS, mutual-TLS or cert-based auth may break unless the customer either: (A) performs inspection before TLS termination (i.e., their inline device terminates then re-issues certs), or (B) we run a small connector inside their VPC so inspection happens on traffic upstream of Redwood's egress.

Tom (Solutions): For POC options:
- Option 1: PrivateLink + customer retains TLS passthrough (no inspect)
- Option 2: PrivateLink + connector VM inside their VPC that forwards to Redwood (preserves logs + allows DPI).

Jin (NetOps): Firewall snippet to paste (minimal):
```
# ShadowBank -> Redwood POC allowlist
# Replace <REDFW_EGRESS> with IPs we provide
ALLOW tcp from 10.10.20.0/24 to <PRIV_LINK_ENI_RANGE> port 443
ALLOW tcp from <connector_subnets> to <REDFW_EGRESS> ports 443
ALLOW udp from <connector_subnets> to 169.254.169.254 port 80 # IMDS if needed
ALLOW udp from <connector_subnets> to 169.254.169.123 port 123 # NTP
```

Jin (NetOps): Note: for PrivateLink the customer sees ENIs in their subnets. Our egress to models will come from managed egress IPs — we can provide a static /32 or a small HA pair.

Priya (Security): Add these bullets for their questionnaire:
- TLS: we enforce TLS1.2+; mTLS available for connector deployments.
- Data retention: request-driven, default retention minimal; logs can be exported to customer-managed S3 in Private deployments.
- Inspection: if customer performs TLS-inspect, mutual-auth may be impacted; recommended: connector inside VPC or a documented cert re-issue flow.

Tom (Solutions): Pricing headliners for packet: static egress IP add-on = ~$2k/month per IP (estimate), connector VM = ~$500/mo + $1.2k one-time setup. Dedicated reserved capacity available if they need lots of static IPs or throughput (starting ~ $20k/mo, sizing TBC). These are placeholders until quotes issued.

Aisha (AE): Perfect. Action items: Tom will send formal IP list + confirmed pricing by EOD Tue. Jin to attach a one-page network sketch for the packet. Priya to write a 2-line security blurb we can paste. I'll schedule kickoff. deploy-bot: New ticket POC-502 created. :white_check_mark:
